subject: Next steps: dedicated capacity sizing call & demo — EmeraldPay
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@emeraldpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + proposal for next step (dedicated sizing + demo)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for today's call. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path forward so we can get your team into a sizing slot next week:

Summary of discovery (what we captured):
- Primary workload: user-facing fraud scoring + enrichment via batch + low-latency API for risk checks
- Expected peak qps: ~280 requests/sec during peak windows (bursty, ~3–5 min bursts)
- Typical request payload: 1–2 KB, average response tokens ~45
- SLO targets: 95th percentile latency < 120ms for the real-time path; batch can be seconds
- Data residency: US region; no PII persisted outside the VPC

Proposed next step:
1) Book a 60–75 minute dedicated capacity sizing + technical deep dive with our infra SE (Karthik) to validate throughput numbers, KV/cache behavior, and to lay out a recommended Dedicated pool config.
2) Short demo (15–20m) of the request-level observability and autoscaling controls we mentioned — we can pair it with the sizing session or run right after.

Proposed times (PT):
- Wed May 5, 10:00–11:15 — ideal for a paired sizing + demo slot
- Thu May 6, 13:30–14:45 — fallback
- Fri May 7, 09:00–10:15 — another option

Prep from EmeraldPay (helps us move quickly):
- A short CSV with representative request rates by minute for a weekday peak window (if you have it)
- Any special model variants / quantization constraints we should know about

I'll loop Karthik in for scheduling and technical prep. If those windows don't work, share a couple of preferred slots and your timezone.

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_playbook.pdf (overview), sizing-checklist.md (link included in drive)
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@emeraldpay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: sales_ops@emeraldpay.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 15:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposal for next step (dedicated sizing + demo)

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the fast recap and clear next steps — that matches our notes. We can definitely prioritize the sizing session. A few clarifications from our side before locking a time:

- The 280 qps number is the peak across our multi-tenant front end; for the call we can provide a minute-level breakdown (we have a CSV export from our load tests).
- We currently run two model variants: v1 (full-fp) and v1_quant (8-bit) in test. We prefer quantized in prod but need perf verification on the higher concurrency path.
- Regarding data residency — yes, US only; we will share the SOC2 summary separately with your security contact.

Our availability: Wed May 5 at 10:00 PT works for the core team (me + one engineer). If possible, please include Karthik and any runtime engineer who can speak to batching and autoscaling.

I'll attach the load-profile export to this thread and include sales_ops in case procurement wants to hop on the call.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | EmeraldPay
emily.turner@emeraldpay.com

Attachments: emeraldpay_load_profile.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@emeraldpay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 08:02:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposal for next step (dedicated sizing + demo)

Thanks Emily — glad the slot works. A couple quick asks to make the sizing session productive:

1) If you can, send a minute-level CSV for a 10–15 minute peak window + one representative off-peak window. That lets us model KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency.
2) In the call we'll validate: concurrency targets, typical seq length (prompt + response), tokenization surprises (long metadata fields), and whether you need guaranteed reserved capacity or burstable commit.
3) Can you confirm whether the API path uses a synchronous call per user action (low latency) vs an async job pattern for enrichment? We treat these differently when sizing pools.

I can join Wednesday at 10:00 PT. I'll bring a recommended rack-of-three pool config to start (rough sketch) and run a quick micro-benchmark in the session if we pin down a representative request.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
